plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch-adjusted DESeq2
plan.analytical_narrative: The data profile gives 12 kidney RNA-seq samples (6 treated, 6 control) from salmon-derived gene-level counts, with two known processing batches balanced across conditions (each batch holds both conditions). Because the batch is a known, balanced confound-free covariate, the correct approach is to include it as a fixed term in the DESeq2 design (~batch + condition) rather than pre-adjusting counts, which would break the count model's mean-variance relationship and risk overstating confidence downstream. The plan follows the grounded procedure from the knowledge service: (1) sample-structure QC to confirm batch does not dominate the primary axis of variance and to catch outliers, (2) minimal low-count pre-filtering, (3) DESeq2 Wald test on the batch-adjusted design with apeglm shrinkage of the condition coefficient, (4) BH-adjusted significance calling with independent filtering, (5) preranked fgsea enrichment against MSigDB Hallmark (locally staged, human, 2026.1) and Reactome (locally staged, current release) using the Wald statistic as the ranking metric, and (6) a consolidated report with fit diagnostics, the p-value histogram, and a full reproducibility record. No translational/clinical-response elements apply — this is a plain two-group DE + pathway question with a batch covariate, not a drug, biomarker, or outcome study.

apeglm shrinkage of the condition coefficient
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
DE + enrichment report with diagnostics, reproducibility record
